config.title: Flex shorthand and patterns

intro.title: Flex shorthand and patterns
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple, responsive webpage layout using CSS Flexbox. You will learn the core concept of the flex shorthand property, which combines flex-grow, flex-shrink, and flex-basis into a single declaration. The main technologies involved are CSS and the Flexbox layout model. By applying common flex patterns, you'll create flexible containers and items that adjust to different screen sizes. This will help you write cleaner, more efficient CSS for modern web designs.
intro.usecase: Flex shorthand is essential for building responsive, component-based layouts in modern web applications. Developers use it daily to quickly arrange navigation bars, card grids, and dashboard panels that adapt to different screen sizes. For example, a product listing page on an e-commerce site uses flex shorthand to align product cards in a grid, ensuring consistent spacing and alignment. Similarly, a settings panel in a web app relies on flex patterns to stack form labels and inputs neatly, improving readability and user interaction.

objectives: Apply flex shorthand properties to configure container behavior in one declaration
Construct responsive layouts using flex-grow, flex-shrink, and flex-basis patterns
Implement flex-direction and flex-wrap combinations for different content flows
Manipulate flex item alignment using justify-content and align-items shorthand patterns
Configure complex flex containers by combining multiple shorthand properties
Update existing layouts by replacing verbose flex properties with shorthand equivalents
Integrate flex shorthand with other CSS properties to create cohesive designs

steps.title: Create a container element with display: flex
steps.instruction: Create a CSS rule for a class named 'container' that sets the display property to flex.
steps.hint: Start by writing a CSS selector for the class 'container', then add the display property with the value 'flex'.
steps.seedCode: /* Write your CSS rule for the .container class here */
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS rule that defines a flex container with the class 'container'.
successCriteria: The .container class selector exists and has display: flex; set.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've correctly written the CSS rule with the class selector and display property.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. Remember to create a CSS rule for the class 'container' and set display to flex.

steps.title: Add flex-direction to control main axis direction
steps.instruction: Add a flex-direction property to the .container rule and set its value to row.
steps.hint: The flex-direction property determines the direction of the main axis. Use 'row' to arrange items horizontally from left to right.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .container rule now includes flex-direction: row, which sets the main axis direction to horizontal.
successCriteria: The .container rule contains the flex-direction property with the value row.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added the flex-direction property with the exact value 'row'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The flex-direction property with value 'row' is missing from the .container rule. Please add it.

steps.title: Add flex-wrap to control item wrapping
steps.instruction: Add the flex-wrap property to the .container selector and set its value to nowrap.
steps.hint: The flex-wrap property controls whether flex items are forced onto one line or can wrap onto multiple lines. Use nowrap to keep all items on a single line.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .container selector now includes flex-wrap: nowrap; to prevent items from wrapping to new lines.
successCriteria: The .container selector contains the flex-wrap property with the value nowrap.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added flex-wrap, but check the value. It should be set to nowrap to prevent wrapping.
steps.feedbackWrong: The flex-wrap property is missing or incorrect. Add flex-wrap: nowrap; to the .container selector.

steps.title: Combine flex-direction and flex-wrap with flex-flow shorthand
steps.instruction: Replace the existing flex-direction and flex-wrap properties with the flex-flow shorthand property, setting it to 'row nowrap'.
steps.hint: The flex-flow property combines flex-direction and flex-wrap. Use 'flex-flow: row nowrap;' to achieve the same layout.
steps.expectedOutcome: The container will use flex-flow shorthand to control both direction and wrapping in one line.
successCriteria: The flex-direction and flex-wrap properties are replaced with flex-flow: row nowrap;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the flex-flow property with both direction and wrap values.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the syntax: you need to replace both properties with 'flex-flow: row nowrap;'.

steps.title: Add justify-content to align items on main axis
steps.instruction: Add the justify-content property to the .container selector with a value of flex-start.
steps.hint: The justify-content property controls how flex items are distributed along the main axis. Use the value flex-start to align items at the start of the main axis.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .container selector now includes the justify-content property set to flex-start, which will align flex items at the start of the main axis.
successCriteria: The .container selector contains the justify-content property with the value flex-start.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a justify-content property, but check that the value is exactly flex-start.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .container selector should include justify-content: flex-start. Review the hint and try again.

steps.title: Add align-items to align items on cross axis
steps.instruction: Add the align-items property to the .container rule with the value stretch to align items along the cross axis.
steps.hint: The align-items property controls how flex items are aligned along the cross axis (perpendicular to the main axis). Use the value stretch to make items fill the container's cross axis.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .container rule will have align-items: stretch; added, which will make flex items stretch to fill the container's cross axis by default.
successCriteria: The .container rule contains the align-items property with the value stretch.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added an align-items property, but check that the value is exactly 'stretch' (without quotes).
steps.feedbackWrong: The align-items property with value stretch is missing from the .container rule. Add it to control cross-axis alignment.

steps.title: Create flex items with basic sizing
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for a class named '.item' that sets width to 100px, height to 100px, and background color to lightblue.
steps.hint: Define a new CSS selector for the item class and add the three properties inside curly braces.
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS rule for .item with width, height, and background-color properties is added.
successCriteria: The .item selector exists with width: 100px, height: 100px, and background-color: lightblue.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some properties, but make sure all three (width, height, and background-color) are present with the correct values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .item rule is missing or incomplete. Check that you've defined the selector and added all three required properties.

steps.title: Add flex-grow to control item expansion
steps.instruction: Add a flex-grow property to the .item rule with a value of 1.
steps.hint: The flex-grow property controls how much a flex item grows relative to other items. A value of 1 means it will take up available space equally.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .item rule now includes flex-grow: 1, allowing items to expand to fill available space.
successCriteria: The .item rule contains the flex-grow property with a value of 1.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added the flex-grow property with the correct value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The flex-grow property wasn't added correctly. Check that you've added it to the .item rule with a value of 1.

steps.title: Add flex-shrink to control item contraction
steps.instruction: Add a flex-shrink property to the .item rule to control how items shrink when the container is too small.
steps.hint: The flex-shrink property determines how much an item will shrink relative to other items when there isn't enough space. A value of 0 prevents shrinking, while higher values shrink more.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .item rule will include a flex-shrink property to control how items contract when space is limited.
successCriteria: The .item rule contains a flex-shrink property with a valid numeric value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to add the flex-shrink property to the .item rule with a numeric value like 0, 1, or 2.
steps.feedbackWrong: The flex-shrink property wasn't properly added. Remember to add 'flex-shrink: [value];' inside the .item rule to control item contraction.

steps.title: Combine flex-grow, flex-shrink, and flex-basis with flex shorthand
steps.instruction: In the .item rule, replace the flex-grow property and the flex-shrink comment with a single flex shorthand property that sets flex-grow to 1, flex-shrink to 1, and flex-basis to auto.
steps.hint: The flex shorthand property accepts three values in order: flex-grow, flex-shrink, and flex-basis. For example: flex: 1 1 auto;
steps.expectedOutcome: The .item rule should use the flex shorthand property instead of separate flex-grow and flex-shrink properties.
successCriteria: The .item rule contains a flex property with three values (e.g., flex: 1 1 auto;) and no longer has separate flex-grow or flex-shrink properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've replaced both the flex-grow property and the flex-shrink comment with a single flex property containing three values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .item rule should use the flex shorthand property with three values (e.g., flex: 1 1 auto;) instead of separate flex-grow and flex-shrink properties.
